title.narrative: Policy and legal framework established and implemented to progressively eliminate child labour

description.narrative: The assessment carried out on the child labour situation in Somalia, established that children living in different parts of the country engage in different types of work. For example, children who live in rural parts of the country are mainly engaged in agricultural activities including farming tasks, and herding livestock. Also, they are forced to join militia groups that control majority of the rural villages where there is insecurity and where they don’t have other alternatives. To redress the situation, the assessment conducted in 2021 provided a number of recommendations that need to be implemented by the government, the social partners and other concerned national and international partners. The Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs has called on ILO’s support for the provision of technical assistance to put into action some of the recommendations of the above-mentioned assessment. Following the realization that the country is returning back to relative peace and is preparing to take control of governance and country’s management, it is agreed that it is important to proceed to address the main challenges in a coordinated manner. In this context, ILO through the CPO129 is supporting the Government of Somalia put in place a mechanism for effective elimination of Child Labour in Somalia and the development of a National Action Plan. As a strategy the ILO is engaging a national consultant to work on the policy draft and put together an action plan following a consultative meeting with the key stakeholders involved. In addition, the envisaged action also considers promotion for the ratification of C138 on minimum age.
